title: Morphisms between completions are the limit of sections of the sheaf Hom modulo powers of the ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, with the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, the notation $\mathcal I^n\mathcal M$ and the completion functor $\mathcal M\mapsto\mathcal M^\wedge=(\mathcal M/\mathcal I^n\mathcal M)_{n\ge1}$ of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ the sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and $\pi_n:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ the quotient maps. For $n\ge1$ the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\mathcal H\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$, $\varphi\mapsto\pi_n\circ\varphi$, vanishes on $\mathcal I^n\mathcal H$ (as $\mathcal I^n$ annihilates $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$), and every local map $\mathcal G\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ vanishes on $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G$; taking global sections one gets maps $\varepsilon_n:\Gamma(X,\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$, compatible with the maps induced by the surjections $\mathcal H/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal H\to\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H$ and with reduction of maps modulo $\mathcal I^n$. Hence a compatible sequence $(s_n)_n\in\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)$ gives a morphism $(\varepsilon_n(s_n))_n:\mathcal G^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. Then the resulting map $$\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)$$ is bijective.

proof.text: (The maps $\varepsilon_n$ and their compatibilities.) Write $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G_n=\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G$, $\mathcal H_n=\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H$ with the quotient maps $\pi_n=q^{\mathcal F}_n$, $q^{\mathcal G}_n$, $q^{\mathcal H}_n$ (cokernels of the inclusions of $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$, $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G$, $\mathcal I^n\mathcal H$), and $p_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$, $p_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ the canonical transition maps, so that $\mathcal F^\wedge=(\mathcal F_n)$, $\mathcal G^\wedge=(\mathcal G_n)$ are objects of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2); in particular $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$. (a) By the definition of $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ as the image of $\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the local sections of $\mathcal I^n\mathcal P$ (any $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal P$) are locally finite sums of products $as$ with $a$ a local section of $\mathcal I^n$ and $s$ of $\mathcal P$; and for an open $V$, $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal P)|_V=(\mathcal I|_V)^n(\mathcal P|_V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (3) (for quasi-coherent $\mathcal P$; the sheaves here are coherent, hence quasi-coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], $X$ being locally Noetherian, and $\mathcal H$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent]). (b) Every $\mathcal O_V$-linear $\psi:\mathcal G|_V\to\mathcal F_n|_V$ sends a product $as$ ($a\in\mathcal I^n(W)$, $s\in\mathcal G(W)$, $W\subseteq V$) to $a\psi(s)\in(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n)(W)=0$, so by (a) $\psi$ kills $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G|_V$ and factors uniquely through the cokernel $q^{\mathcal G}_n|_V$; hence precomposition with $q^{\mathcal G}_n$ is a bijection $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)(V)\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_n)(V)$, compatible with restriction and $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear, i.e. an isomorphism of sheaves Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. (c) $\varphi\mapsto\pi_n\circ\varphi$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism $\mathcal H\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_n)$ compatible with restriction; it kills each product $a\varphi$ with $a\in\mathcal I^n(W)$, as $\pi_n\circ(a\varphi)=a(\pi_n\circ\varphi)$ has values in $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$, hence by (a) kills $\mathcal I^n\mathcal H$ and factors uniquely through $q^{\mathcal H}_n$. Composing with the inverse of (b) gives a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $e_n:\mathcal H_n\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$ with $e_n(\varphi\bmod\mathcal I^n)$ the map $\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n$ induced by $\pi_n\circ\varphi$; $\varepsilon_n=\Gamma(X,e_n)$. (d) For $\alpha\in\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_{n+1},\mathcal F_{n+1})(V)$, $p_n\circ\alpha$ kills $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G_{n+1}$ (as in (b)), and $p_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ is the cokernel of $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1), so there is a unique $\rho_n(\alpha)$ with $p_n\circ\alpha=\rho_n(\alpha)\circ p_n$; $\rho_n$ is a morphism of sheaves, and a family $(\alpha_n)$, $\alpha_n\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$, is a morphism $\mathcal G^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ iff $\rho_n(\alpha_{n+1})=\alpha_n$ for all $n$. With $t_n:\mathcal H_{n+1}\to\mathcal H_n$ the transition map, $\rho_n\circ e_{n+1}=e_n\circ t_n$: both are determined by their composites with the epimorphism $q^{\mathcal H}_{n+1}$, and both send $\varphi$ to the map induced by $p_n\pi_{n+1}\varphi=\pi_n\varphi$. So $\Phi:(s_n)_n\mapsto(\varepsilon_n(s_n))_n$ is a well defined map $\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal H_n)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)$. (e) For an affine open $U\subseteq X$, $U$ is a Noetherian scheme (step 2), and the same construction for $(U,\mathcal I|_U,\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal G|_U)$, whose sheaf Hom is $\mathcal H|_U$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and whose quotients are $\mathcal H_n|_U$ etc. by (a), gives $\Phi_U$ with $\Phi_U((s_n|_U)_n)=\Phi((s_n)_n)|_U$ (componentwise restriction of maps), since $e_n$ is a morphism of sheaves.

proof.text: (Affine opens: the modules.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, so $(U,\mathcal O_X|_U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. As $X$ is locally Noetherian, $A$ is Noetherian [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]; so $U$ is a Noetherian scheme. Put $I=\mathcal I(U)$; as $\mathcal I|_U$ is quasi-coherent, the counit $\widetilde I\to\mathcal I|_U$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3), so $(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ is the situation of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] for $(A,I)$. The sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ are coherent ([lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent] for $\mathcal H$), hence quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so $M=\mathcal F(U)$, $N=\mathcal G(U)$ and $\mathcal H(U)$ are finitely generated $A$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a), and $\mathcal F_n(U)=M/I^nM$, $\mathcal G_n(U)=N/I^nN$, $\mathcal H_n(U)=\mathcal H(U)/I^n\mathcal H(U)$ with $q_n(U)$ the quotient maps [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2). By full faithfulness of $\Gamma(U,-)$ on quasi-coherent modules over the affine $U$ ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (1),(3): $\alpha\mapsto\Gamma(U,\alpha)$ is the adjunction bijection composed with the counit isomorphism), $\mathcal H(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G|_U,\mathcal F|_U)\to H:=\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,M)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_U$, is an $A$-linear bijection (so $H$ is a finitely generated $A$-module), and likewise $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(N/I^nN,M/I^nM)$. Under these identifications $\mathcal H_n(U)=H/I^nH$ and $e_n(U)$ of step 1 is $h\bmod I^nH\mapsto\bar h_n$, where $\bar h_n(x\bmod I^nN)=h(x)\bmod I^nM$ (evaluate on sections over $U$, where $q^{\mathcal H}_n(U)$ is surjective). Hence $\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_n)=\varprojlim_nH/I^nH=H^\wedge$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0882 (lemma-completion-internal-hom, line 6438), proof, first sentences: 'we may assume X = Spec(A) and F, G given by finite A-modules ... H corresponds to the finite A-module H = Hom_A(M, N)'

proof.text: (Affine opens: reduction to modules over $A^\wedge$.) Keep the notation of step 2 and let $E:\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)$, $(\mathcal P_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal P_n)$, $(\alpha_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\alpha_n)$, be the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2); in particular $E$ is bijective on Hom sets. By step 2, $E(\mathcal G^\wedge|_U)=\varprojlim N/I^nN=N^\wedge$ and $E(\mathcal F^\wedge|_U)=M^\wedge$ (with $A^\wedge$ acting componentwise), and $E\circ\Phi_U:H^\wedge\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$ is $$\beta:(h_n\bmod I^nH)_n\longmapsto\big((x_n\bmod I^nN)_n\mapsto(h_n(x_n)\bmod I^nM)_n\big).$$ Hence $\Phi_U$ is bijective if and only if $\beta$ is. Note that $\beta$ is $A^\wedge$-linear: $\beta((a_n)_n(h_n)_n)$ and $(a_n)_n\beta((h_n)_n)$ both send $(x_n)$ to $(a_nh_n(x_n))_n$; and for $h\in H$, $\beta(\iota_H(h))=h^\wedge:(x_n)_n\mapsto(h(x_n))_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0882 (lemma-completion-internal-hom, line 6438), proof: 'The statement of the lemma becomes the statement H^ = Hom_{A^}(M^, N^) via the equivalence of Lemma 087W'

proof.text: (Affine opens: $\beta$ is bijective.) $A$ is Noetherian and $N$, $M$, $H$ are finitely generated $A$-modules (step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] (2) the $A^\wedge$-linear maps $c_P:A^\wedge\otimes_AP\to P^\wedge$, $a\otimes x\mapsto a\,\iota_P(x)$, are bijective for $P=N,M,H$. The ring map $A\to A^\wedge$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], and $N$ is finitely generated over the Noetherian $A$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] the map $\theta:A^\wedge\otimes_AH\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(A^\wedge\otimes_AN,A^\wedge\otimes_AM)$, $a\otimes h\mapsto a(\mathrm{id}\otimes h)$, is bijective. Let $\gamma:\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(A^\wedge\otimes_AN,A^\wedge\otimes_AM)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$, $f\mapsto c_M\circ f\circ c_N^{-1}$, a bijection. Both $\beta\circ c_H$ and $\gamma\circ\theta$ are $A^\wedge$-linear (step 3), and $A^\wedge\otimes_AH$ is generated as an $A^\wedge$-module by the $1\otimes h$; on these, $\beta(c_H(1\otimes h))=\beta(\iota_H(h))=h^\wedge$ (step 3) and $\gamma(\theta(1\otimes h))=c_M\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes h)\circ c_N^{-1}=h^\wedge$ by the naturality $h^\wedge\circ c_N=c_M\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes h)$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] (1). Hence $\beta=\gamma\circ\theta\circ c_H^{-1}$ is bijective, and by step 3 so is $\Phi_U$, for every affine open $U\subseteq X$. (This is Stacks' chain $H^\wedge=H\otimes_AA^\wedge=\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N\otimes_AA^\wedge,M\otimes_AA^\wedge)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$, with the check that it is the map $\beta$.)

proof.text: (From affine opens to $X$.) The affine opens of $X$ form a basis of its topology, and $\mathcal H_n$ and $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$ are sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Injectivity of $\Phi$: if $\Phi(s)=\Phi(s')$ then for every affine open $U$, $\Phi_U(s|_U)=\Phi(s)|_U=\Phi(s')|_U=\Phi_U(s'|_U)$ (step 1 (e)), so $s_n|_U=s'_n|_U$ for all $n$ (step 4), and $s_n=s'_n$ as the affine opens cover $X$. Surjectivity: let $\alpha=(\alpha_n)$ be a morphism $\mathcal G^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge$. For each affine open $U$ choose (step 4) $t^U\in\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_n)$ with $\Phi_U(t^U)=\alpha|_U$. For affine opens $U,V$ and an affine open $W\subseteq U\cap V$, $\Phi_W(t^U|_W)=\alpha|_W=\Phi_W(t^V|_W)$ (step 1 (e), applied on $U$ and on $V$), so $t^U_n|_W=t^V_n|_W$ (step 4); such $W$ cover $U\cap V$, so $t^U_n$ and $t^V_n$ agree on $U\cap V$ and glue to $s_n\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal H_n)$. The relation $t_n(s_{n+1})=s_n$ holds on every affine $U$, hence on $X$; so $s=(s_n)\in\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal H_n)$, and $\Phi(s)_n$ and $\alpha_n$ are sections of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$ with the same restriction $\Phi_U(t^U)_n=\alpha_n|_U$ to every affine $U$, hence equal. So $\Phi$ is bijective.
